_comment: Snapy app strings (English). Source of truth: core/i18n/en.json — copy with `dart run tool/sync_core.dart`. {name} = filled in by the app. Kind, non-judgemental wording only.

home.tagline: Tap the pill — here or at the top of any app — to talk to Snapy.

rc.setup_sub: See your screen time and how many reels you’ve watched, right beside your camera.
rc.step_usage_sub: Screen time per app, the same data as Digital Wellbeing
rc.step_counter_sub: Counts reels and shows the chip over other apps
rc.counter_off: Turn on the Reel counter for reel numbers

chip.desc: Snapy Real Count: {time} today, {reels} reels. Tap to talk to Snapy, long-press for quick actions, swipe down for today’s apps.

nudge.session_reels: {n} Reels in {min} min. Keep going or take a 2-min reset?
nudge.session_reels_soft: {n} reels so far. A 2-minute reset is here if you want it.
nudge.frequent_opens: You keep coming back to {app}. Stuck on something? I can start a {focus}-min focus.
nudge.frequent_opens_soft: {app} again. A {focus}-min focus is one tap away.
nudge.soft_limit: You’ve reached the time you set for {app} today. Take a 2-min reset?
nudge.soft_limit_soft: That’s the {app} time you planned for today. Your call.
nudge.bedtime: It’s getting late. Wind down for tonight?
nudge.bedtime_soft: Late night. Sleep well whenever you’re ready.
nudge.bedtime_task: It’s getting late. Tomorrow starts with: {task}. Wind down?
nudge.bedtime_task_soft: Tomorrow starts with: {task}. Sleep well whenever you’re ready.
nudge.focus_open: You’re in focus until {until}. Open {app} anyway?
nudge.intention_done_dms: Your {minutes} min for DMs is up. Wrap up?
nudge.intention_done_post: Your {minutes} min to post is up. Wrap up?
nudge.intention_done_browse: Your {minutes} min of browsing is up. Wrap up?

intent.title: What are you here for?
intent.set: Okay — I’ll check in after {minutes} min.

break.title: A 10-second pause
break.sub: You set a limit for {app}. Take a breath — then it’s your call.

focus.notif_text: Snapy will check in if a social app opens.

report.title: Your week
report.less: {pct}% less screen time than your last week.
report.more: {pct}% more than your last week. A new week is a fresh start.
report.same: About the same as your last week.
report.first: Your first week with Snapy. Next Sunday you’ll see how it compares.
report.only_you: Compared only with your own last week.

three.title: Today’s three
three.ask: What are 3 things that matter today?
three.later: Tomorrow morning I’ll ask for your three.

streak.title: Streak
streak.forgiven: One miss forgiven this week. The streak lives on.
streak.rule: A day counts when one of your three is done, or you stay within the limits you set. One miss a week is forgiven.

privacy.title: Privacy receipts
privacy.note: Snapy keeps your data on this phone. Here is every file it saved and every request it made this month. Tap the bin to delete one.

sent_kind.rules_check: Checked for counter rule updates (nothing about you)

battery.title: Keep the counter running
battery.sub: Some phones stop apps in the background to save battery. That stops the chip and the Reel counter. Two minutes here fixes it.
battery.not_found: This phone didn’t open that screen. Follow the steps above in Settings.
battery.ok: Battery optimisation is off for Snapy.
battery.on: Battery optimisation is on for Snapy.

xiaomi.name: Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO (MIUI / HyperOS)
steps: Settings → Apps → Manage apps → Snapy → turn on Autostart.
Open Recents, pull Snapy down and tap the lock.

oppo.name: Oppo, Realme (ColorOS / realme UI)
steps: Settings → Battery → App battery management → Snapy → Allow background activity.
Settings → Apps → Auto launch → turn on Snapy.

vivo.name: Vivo, iQOO (Funtouch / OriginOS)
steps: Settings → Battery → Background power consumption → Snapy → Allow.
i Manager → App manager → Autostart → turn on Snapy.

samsung.name: Samsung (One UI)
steps: Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → keep Snapy out of Sleeping and Deep sleeping apps.
Add Snapy to Never sleeping apps.

oneplus.name: OnePlus (OxygenOS)
steps: Settings → Apps → Snapy → Battery → Allow background activity.
Settings → Battery → Battery optimisation → Snapy → Don’t optimise.

other.name: Other phones
steps: Settings → Apps → Snapy → Battery → Unrestricted (or Don’t optimise).

perm.title: Set up Snapy
perm.sub: Each step says why. Skip any of them — Snapy still works, just with less.
perm.done_sub: You can change any of this later in Settings.

usage.title: Usage access
usage.why: Shows your screen time per app — the same numbers as Digital Wellbeing. It stays on your phone.
usage.without: Without it: no screen time in the chip.

overlay.title: Display over other apps
overlay.why: Lets the chip sit by your camera over other apps, even when the Reel counter is off.
overlay.without: Without it: the chip only shows while the Reel counter is on.

counter.title: Reel counter
counter.disclosure: Count Reels and Shorts. Never reads messages or what you type.
counter.detail:
Snapy uses Android’s Accessibility permission to:
• see which app is open, to show your screen time in the chip
• count swipes in short-video feeds (Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Facebook, Snapchat, Moj, Josh and more)
• go Back, Home or open Recents when you ask by voice, and tap Send when you confirm a WhatsApp message

Everything is counted on your phone. Snapy never reads, stores or sends your messages, posts, passwords or anything you type, and nothing is uploaded.

On the next screen, tap “Snapy Real Count” and turn it on.
counter.without: Without it: screen time only, no reel numbers.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.why: Reminders, your Sunday report and the morning “three things”.
notifications.without: Without them: reminders only show inside Snapy.

mic.title: Microphone and “Hey Snapy” (optional)
mic.why: Talk to Snapy. With “Hey Snapy” on, a small model on your phone listens only for its name. Audio never leaves the phone.
mic.without: Without it: type to Snapy instead.

contacts.title: Contacts and calls (later)
contacts.why: Not now. Snapy asks the first time you say something like “call Mom” or “WhatsApp Rahul”.

rcset.title: Chip & nudges
rcset.chip_sub: Screen time and reels beside your camera. Drag it anywhere.
rcset.overlay_fallback: Show the chip when the Reel counter is off
rcset.overlay_fallback_sub: Uses “Display over other apps” and a small notification.
rcset.style_sub: “On the camera” wraps the chip around the camera with a limit ring. Takes effect the next time the Reel counter starts.
rcset.reset_position: Put it back on the camera
rcset.nudges_sub: At most one every {min} minutes. Never during calls or navigation.
rcset.intention_sub: When a social app opens: DMs, post, or browse for a few minutes.
rcset.creator: Creator mode
rcset.creator_sub: Posting, editing and DMs don’t count — only feeds do.
rcset.break_sub: Before a social app opens again after its limit. Off unless you turn it on.
rcset.simple_sub: Larger chip and text, fewer options.
rcset.reports_sub: Prepare anonymous app-version reports when I say the counter looks wrong.

wrong.title: Counter looks wrong?
wrong.body: Snapy can prepare an anonymous report: Snapy’s version, Android version, phone brand and the versions of the apps it counts. No account, no counts, nothing you watched.
wrong.prepared: Report saved on this phone. Sending isn’t available yet, so nothing was sent.
wrong.opt_in: Turn on Counter reports in Chip & nudges first.

notif.chip_text: Shows your screen time over other apps. Turn off in Snapy → Chip & nudges.
notif.wake_text: Your phone restarted. Tap to listen for “Hey Snapy” again.
